turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come, sit. Pulse is one hundred and eighteen, that is fast. BP is one thirty over eighty four, temperature thirty seven point two. Oxygen ninety eight percent and the breathing is eighteen.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh, the pulse is always a bit fast only. I walked up from the parking, it is nothing.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Mm. A short walk will not give one hundred and eighteen. My own sister had her thyroid taken out last year, so fast pulses catch my eye, but that is her matter.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good morning. I am Dr. Menon. What brought you today?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Weight is coming down. The shirts are loose. My wife forced the visit, but it is not a big thing, doctor.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Weight coming down. Since when, and roughly how many kilos?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, two three months. I cannot say the exact date it started. Maybe four five kilos, I don't weigh myself daily.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the appetite, in these months?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): More only, actually. Second helping, evening snacks. If you eat you should gain, no? I am fine as such.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any racing of the heart, sweating, or shaking in the hands?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Heart races sometimes, evenings mostly. A little sweating, I wipe my face and carry on. Hands shake a bit when I hold the cup, not always. Very minor.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is that shaking painful?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not painful.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): What about fever, or loose motions?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Never any fever. Loose motions, not really.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any long-standing problem, BP, sugar, asthma?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Asthma, five-ish years. It is quiet, I manage. No BP, no sugar.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): With the asthma, are you getting any wheeze these days?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No... well, sometimes. At night only, a small whistle. I don't bother with it.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): And chest tightness?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Not that either.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tell me the medicines you take.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Monteleukast, ten milligram, one tablet at night. And salbutemol pump, hundred microgram, two puffs if I need. I skip the night tablet some days, I just forget.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines or to food?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Family history, thyroid, heart, anything in siblings or parents?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Elder sister has thyroid. She takes tablets for it since long. Parents are okay as such.
[SEG0030] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor, the ECG room is free after this. I must leave by four, my boy is at home with a bad cough.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright, let me examine. The pulse is fast but regular, and there is a fine tremor in both hands. The thyroid does not feel enlarged. Lungs are clear, no wheeze just now.

[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. Let me say it back. Weight down over two to three months, eating more, heart racing, some sweating, shaky hands, a little night wheeze, asthma for about five years, sister with thyroid. No chest pain, no fever, no loose motions, no chest tightness, the shake is not painful, and no allergy.

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am thinking it through, not jumping. If the thyroid pours out too much hormone, the metabolism speeds up, so the heart runs fast and the weight falls even while you are eating more. Anxiety can copy that same picture. I will not decide which one it is today.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): It will be the project only. I am a software engineer, long hours. I am okay, really.

[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Work stress stays on the list. I am not calling this anxiety and closing the file. I am booking blood tests today, thyroid panel, full blood count and sugar, and an ECG, and they are arranged.

[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): No new tablet from me until those reports. Kindly continue the monteleukast every night and the pump when you need it, and try not to skip. Come back in one week and we will go over the results. If you get bad chest pain or you feel faint before that, go to emergency, don't sit on it.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): One week is okay. I don't want extra tablets anyway.
[SEG0038] person_4 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I will book the blood draw and the ECG for today itself, and the review with doctor in one week. Kindly collect the slip at the desk.

spec.situation: Younger adult losing weight with a fast heartbeat, sweating, shaky hands, eats more than usual; hair thinning not mentioned; a sister has thyroid disease; blood tests and ECG planned.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

bad.reason: Only shaking is stated not painful; generalized pain absence is unsupported.

omissions.text: Weight loss amount was approximately 4 to 5 kg over 2 to 3 months.
No new medication was prescribed until the test results are available.
Investigations (blood draw and ECG) were to be done today itself, not just planned generally.

There was a real difference in viewpoint: patient felt it was just work/project stress and not a big issue, while doctor said stress/anxiety remains on the list but would not label it anxiety and close the case before testing.
